跟着在东京工作的ヤン，从健身房、羽毛球会、语言交换到祭典、志愿者和婚礼致辞，用日: Follow Yang, who works in Tokyo, from the gym, a badminton club, and language exchange to festivals, volunteering, and a wedding speech, and make true friends in Japanese.
健身房入会和问器械: Joining a gym and asking about the machines
周六上午，来东京工作第二年的ヤン下决心开始运动，走进公司附近一家健身房。前台的工: It's Saturday morning. Yang, now in her second year working in Tokyo, has made up her mind to start exercising and walks into a gym near her office. Sakamoto, a staff member at the front desk, helps her with the membership sign-up, then shows her around the facility, teaches her how to use the treadmill and a chest machine, and goes over a few of the gym's rules along the way.
健身房工作人员，二十多岁，热情爽朗，说话很有礼貌: Gym staff member in his twenties; warm and cheerful, and speaks very politely
在东京IT公司工作的中国人，二十八岁，第一次去日本的健身房: From China, works at an IT company in Tokyo; 28 years old and going to a Japanese gym for the first time
坂本是店员，ヤン是客人。坂本用服务业的敬语「ご入会」「ご案内します」「お願いして: Sakamoto is staff and Yang is a customer. Sakamoto uses service-industry keigo such as 「ご入会」, 「ご案内します」, and 「お願いしています」. For Yang, basic 「です・ます」 is perfectly enough; there's no need to go out of her way to use humble language. When customers also speak politely to staff, Japanese people see them as well-mannered; using plain style right from the start comes across as a bit rude.
欢迎光临。您是来咨询入会的吗？: Welcome. Are you here to ask about a membership?
「ご入会」「ご相談」前面加「ご」，是对客人的尊敬，服务业的标准说法。听到「ご〜で: Adding 「ご」 to 「ご入会」 and 「ご相談」 shows respect for the customer; it's the standard way of speaking in the service industry. When you hear 「ご〜ですか」, you know the staff member is checking why you've come. Just answer 「はい」 and then say what you need. There's no need to be nervous.
是的。我是第一次来，也可以先参观一下吗？: Yes. It's my first time here. Could I also take a look around?
「〜んですが」先交代自己的情况，再提问，语气很软。日本人提要求前很习惯这样「铺垫: 「〜んですが」 explains your situation first and then asks the question, which makes it sound very soft. Japanese people are used to "laying the groundwork" with a line like this before making a request. Simply saying 「見学できますか」 isn't wrong, but adding 「初めてなんですが」 lets the other person know to explain things in more detail.
当然可以。那我先带您进去看看吧。: Of course. Then let me show you around inside first.
这里是跑步机。用这个按钮可以调速度。: This is the treadmill. You can change the speed with this button.
不好意思，那台器械是怎么用的呢？: Excuse me, how do you use that machine?
问用法的万能句。「どうやって使いますか」也可以，但「〜んですか」带着「我真的不懂: An all-purpose phrase for asking how to use something. 「どうやって使いますか」 also works, but 「〜んですか」 carries the nuance of "I really don't know and would like you to show me," so it sounds more natural. If you don't know, ask: that's far better than experimenting on your own and getting hurt. What staff actually worry about most is newcomers who don't ask.
那是练胸的器械。首先在这里选重量。一开始轻一点比较好哦。: That's a machine for working your chest. First, choose the weight here. It's best to go a little light at first.
明白了。用完以后需要做什么吗？: I see. Is there anything I should do after I use it?
主动问「用完之后要做什么」，是在问这里的规矩。日本的健身房很讲究「マナー」，你先: Asking "What should I do after I'm done?" on your own is asking about the rules of the place. Gyms in Japan take 「マナー」 (etiquette) very seriously. Asking first is like telling them "I want to follow the rules," and they'll warm to you right away.
是的，请用旁边配的毛巾把汗擦掉。还有，人多的时候请大家最多用三十分钟。: Yes, please wipe off your sweat with the towels provided. Also, when it's crowded, we ask that you keep it to thirty minutes at most.
「〜をお願いしています」是店家委婉地说规则：不说「禁止」「ダメです」，而说「我们: 「〜をお願いしています」 is how a business states a rule indirectly: instead of saying 「禁止」 or 「ダメです」, they say "we ask everyone to do this." It sounds like a request, but it's actually a rule, and you must follow it.
原来如此。那我入会。月费多少钱？: I see. Then I'll sign up. How much is the monthly fee?
每月八千八百日元。请在这张表上填写姓名和住址。: It's 8,800 yen a month. Please fill in your name and address on this form.
好的。那个，我日语还不太好，不懂的时候可以再来问您吗？: Okay. Um, my Japanese isn't very good yet, so when I don't understand something, may I ask you again?
先说出自己的不足，再请求帮忙。这不是示弱，而是让对方知道该怎么帮你。日本人很少主: Mention what you can't do yet first, then ask for help. This isn't a sign of weakness; it lets the other person know how to help you. Japanese people rarely approach others uninvited and intervene, so when you speak up first, it gives them a "reason" to help you.
当然！随时叫我。我们一起加油吧。: Of course! Feel free to call me over anytime. Let's do our best together!
健身房、俱乐部、协会都用。「入会金」= 入会费，「退会」= 退会: Used for gyms, clubs, and associations. 「入会金」 = joining fee; 「退会」 = canceling one's membership
正式加入前先看看。「見学できますか」「見学だけでも大丈夫ですか」: Taking a look before officially joining. 「見学できますか」 (Can I look around?), 「見学だけでも大丈夫ですか」 (Is it okay if I just look around?)
健身房、兴趣班按月交的费用，读「つきかいひ」不读「げつかいひ」: The fee paid every month at a gym or hobby class. Read 「つきかいひ」, not 「げつかいひ」
「マシンを使う」；跑步机叫「ランニングマシン」或「トレッドミル」: 「マシンを使う」 (to use a machine); a treadmill is called 「ランニングマシン」 or 「トレッドミル」
锻炼（身体某部位）: to train, to strengthen (a part of the body)
「胸を鍛える」「足腰を鍛える」，也可以说「精神を鍛える」: 「胸を鍛える」 (to work one's chest), 「足腰を鍛える」 (to strengthen one's legs and lower back); you can also say 「精神を鍛える」 (to train one's mind)
健身器械上调的就是「重さ」。「重さを選ぶ」「重さを変える」: What you adjust on a gym machine is the 「重さ」. 「重さを選ぶ」 (to choose the weight), 「重さを変える」 (to change the weight)
稍轻一点: on the light side, a little lighter
「〜め」表示「稍微……一点」：「軽めに」「早めに」「少なめに」: 「〜め」 means "slightly ...": 「軽めに」 (a bit lighter), 「早めに」 (a bit early), 「少なめに」 (a bit less)
「備え付けのタオル」「備え付けの消毒液」，意思是可以随便用: 「備え付けのタオル」 (towels provided), 「備え付けの消毒液」 (disinfectant provided): it means you're free to use them
健身房礼仪的头一条：用完器械要擦掉汗: Rule number one of gym etiquette: wipe off your sweat after using a machine
人多、拥挤: to be crowded, to be busy
「混んでいる時」= 人多的时候；反义「空いている」: 「混んでいる時」 = when it's crowded; the opposite is 「空いている」
「申込用紙」= 申请表。「用紙に記入する」= 填表: 「申込用紙」 = application form. 「用紙に記入する」 = to fill in a form
打招呼、叫一声: to speak to (someone), to call out to (someone)
「何かあったら声をかけてください」是店员常说的客气话，真的可以叫: 「何かあったら声をかけてください」 (Let us know if you need anything) is a polite phrase staff often say, and you really can call on them
（先说明情况）……，（再提出请求或问题）: (state the situation first) ..., (then make a request or ask a question)
普通形 + んですが（名词・な形容词 + なんですが）: Plain form + んですが (noun / な-adjective + なんですが)
日本人不爱一上来就提要求，喜欢先把背景交代给对方，再把话递过去。「〜んですが」就: Japanese people don't like to make a request right off the bat; they prefer to give the other person the background first and then pass the actual question over. 「〜んですが」 is that cushion. It works with staff, seniors, and strangers alike; between friends, switch to 「〜んだけど」.
我是第一次来，该怎么做呢？: It's my first time. What should I do?
我忘带毛巾了，可以借吗？: I forgot my towel. Could I borrow one?
どうやって + 动词辞书形 + んですか: どうやって + verb dictionary form + んですか
问方法、问用法最直接的一句。带「んですか」显得你真心想知道、在请教，而不是质问。: The most direct way to ask how to do something or how to use something. Adding 「んですか」 shows that you genuinely want to know and are asking for guidance, not interrogating. You can say it naturally whenever you can't figure out a machine, a ticket machine, or an app.
这台器械怎么用呢？: How do you use this machine?
储物柜怎么锁呢？: How do you close the locker?
动词て形 + もいいですか: Verb て-form + もいいですか
请求许可的基本句。对店员、前辈用「〜てもいいですか」，更客气可以说「〜てもよろし: The basic phrase for asking permission. Use 「〜てもいいですか」 with staff and seniors; to be more polite, you can say 「〜てもよろしいですか」; between friends, say 「〜てもいい？」. When you ask before doing something, Japanese people see you as tactful.
只参观一下可以吗？: Is it all right if I just look around?
不懂的时候可以再问吗？: When I don't understand something, may I ask again?
第一次去健身房、游泳馆、瑜伽馆等地方，和前台、工作人员说话时。先说「初めてなんで: When you're talking to the front desk or staff on your first visit to a gym, swimming pool, yoga studio, or similar place. Start with 「初めてなんですが」 and then ask how to use things and what the rules are, and they'll explain especially carefully.
不要不问就随便用器械，也不要占着器械刷手机。有些中国人觉得「花了钱就随便用」，但: Don't start using machines without asking, and don't hog a machine while scrolling on your phone. Some people think "I paid, so I can use it however I like," but in Japan, if you don't wipe off your sweat or you occupy equipment for a long time, the people around you will quietly remember it.
工作人员听到「わからない時はまた聞いてもいいですか」会很放心：这个人不懂会问，不: When staff hear 「わからない時はまた聞いてもいいですか」, they feel reassured: this person will ask when they don't know something and won't do anything reckless and get hurt. In their eyes, a member who asks about the rules on their own is a "good member," and they'll be all the more willing to look out for you from then on.
日本的健身房看起来大家都闷头练、互不说话，好像很冷淡。其实不是。我刚去的时候把哑: At Japanese gyms, everyone seems to train in silence without talking to each other, which can look cold. It really isn't. When I first started going, I put a dumbbell back on the wrong rack. An older man nearby didn't say anything and quietly put it back for me; the next time we met, though, he smiled and showed me how to do a proper squat. Japanese people don't readily speak up because they're afraid of bothering you. Once you say 「初めてなんです」, others have a reason to help you. Wiping down a machine after you use it and not hogging it when it's busy is being considerate of the next person. And only when you say what you don't understand can others point things out in time, so you can correct yourself sooner. If you pretend to know when you don't, you're the one who gets hurt.
你第一次来健身房，想先看看再决定是否入会，最合适的说法是？: It's your first time at a gym, and you want to look around before deciding whether to join. What's the most appropriate thing to say?
先说明「初めてなんですが」再提出请求，礼貌又清楚。「見せて」「お金はいくら？」是: Explaining 「初めてなんですが」 first and then making your request is polite and clear. 「見せて」 and 「お金はいくら？」 are plain style used between friends, and they sound rude when said to staff.
工作人员说「混んでいる時は三十分までにお願いしています」，这句话的真正意思是？: A staff member says 「混んでいる時は三十分までにお願いしています」. What does this really mean?
人多时最好用三十分钟以上: When it's crowded, it's best to use it for more than thirty minutes
这只是建议，可以不管: It's just a suggestion, so you can ignore it
人多时最多只能用三十分钟，这是规定: When it's crowded, you can use it for thirty minutes at most; it's a rule
三十分钟后要付钱: You have to pay after thirty minutes
「〜をお願いしています」是店家委婉地说规则，听起来是拜托，实际上就是要遵守的规定: 「〜をお願いしています」 is how a business states a rule indirectly. It sounds like a request, but it's actually a rule you're expected to follow.
用完器械，下一步最符合日本健身房礼仪的是？: After using a machine, which next step best fits Japanese gym etiquette?
用备好的毛巾把汗擦掉: Wipe off your sweat with the towels provided
直接走开，工作人员会打扫: Just walk away; the staff will clean up
在器械上休息刷手机: Rest on the machine and scroll on your phone
把重量调到最重: Set the weight to the heaviest
擦掉汗是对下一个使用者的体谅，也是日本健身房最基本的礼仪。: Wiping off your sweat is being considerate of the next person who uses it, and it's the most basic etiquette at Japanese gyms.
